__comment: TAP LONDON food data with personality, vibe, mustTry and tags

items.name: Dishoom Covent Garden
items.description: A London favourite for black daal, grills, breakfast naan rolls, and theatre-district buzz.
items.opinion: Worth every minute of the queue. The black daal alone is worth the trip.

items.name: Padella
items.description: Queue-worthy handmade pasta beside Borough Market; the short menu changes daily.
items.opinion: Possibly the best pasta in London at half the price of anywhere else.

items.name: Flat Iron Soho
items.description: Simple, good-value steak and sides in a lively Soho setting.
items.mustTry: Flat iron steak with dripping sauce
items.opinion: Best value steak in London — no frills, just great beef.

items.name: Kiln
items.description: Wood-fired Thai dishes, clay-pot noodles, and counter seats that make dinner feel alive.
items.opinion: The smoke, the heat, the flavour — Kiln is London dining at its best.

items.name: Brat
items.description: Smoky sharing plates and whole fish from a celebrated open-fire kitchen.
items.opinion: Special occasion territory. The fire-cooked fish is absolutely unforgettable.

items.name: Manteca
items.description: House-made pasta, nose-to-tail cooking, and bold modern Italian near Old Street.
items.opinion: Genuinely exciting cooking — book ahead or you won't get in.

items.name: The Wolseley
items.description: A polished London classic for breakfast, afternoon tea, oysters, and old-school service.
items.opinion: The most glamorous breakfast room in London. Worth dressing up for.

items.name: Roti King
items.description: Fast, comforting Malaysian roti canai, nasi lemak, and curries.
items.opinion: A basement cult classic. Tiny, cheap, and absolutely brilliant.

items.name: Chick 'n' Sours
items.description: Crispy fried chicken, punchy sides, and sour cocktails near the West End.
items.opinion: Best chicken burger in central London — spicy, messy, addictive.

items.name: Maedah Grill
items.description: Reliable halal grills, mezze, and family-friendly seating near East London Mosque.
items.opinion: Consistent, generous, halal — a reliable east London favourite.

items.name: Guanabana
items.description: Colourful halal-friendly plates, jerk flavours, burgers, mocktails, and a lively Camden setting.
items.mustTry: Jerk chicken with rice and peas
items.opinion: Vibrant, colourful and genuinely fun — one of London's most underrated halal spots.

items.name: The Great Chase
items.description: A polished halal dining room for Sunday roasts, tasting menus, and alcohol-free pairings.
items.mustTry: Sunday roast with all the trimmings
items.opinion: Proof that halal fine dining is here. Elegant, considered, and genuinely impressive.

items.name: Etles Uyghur Restaurant
items.description: Hand-pulled noodles, lamb skewers, big-plate chicken, and warm service.
items.mustTry: Big plate chicken with hand-pulled noodles
items.opinion: Nothing else like it in London. The big plate chicken is life-changing.

items.name: Liman Restaurant
items.description: Fresh Turkish dishes, generous sharing plates, and a welcoming neighbourhood feel.
items.opinion: Relaxed, fresh and always good. A reliable halal gem in north London.

items.name: Ranoush Juice
items.description: A quick Edgware Road classic for shawarma, grills, and fresh juices until late.
items.opinion: The shawarma at 2am after a night out hits different. Open very late.

items.name: Maroush Edgware Road
items.description: Well-known Lebanese dining for mezze, grilled meats, and breads near Marble Arch.
items.opinion: Classic, reliable Lebanese. Great for groups and big family meals.

items.name: Tayyabs
items.description: East London institution for sizzling lamb chops, karahi dishes, and lively family dining.
items.mustTry: Lamb chops — order as soon as you sit down
items.opinion: A London institution. The lamb chops are still the best in the city.

items.name: Efes Whitechapel
items.description: Generous Turkish grills, bread, salads, and platters in East London.
items.opinion: Big portions, solid flavours and always open late. East London staple.

items.name: Monmouth Coffee
items.description: A London coffee institution with carefully sourced beans beside Borough Market.
items.opinion: The standard all London coffee is measured against. Non-negotiable.

items.name: Kaffeine
items.description: Excellent flat whites, pastries, and Australian-style cafe energy near Oxford Street.
items.opinion: The best flat white near Oxford Street. Tiny but mighty.

items.name: WatchHouse
items.description: Stylish London coffee with strong espresso, brunch plates, and multiple branches.
items.mustTry: Oat flat white and avocado toast
items.opinion: The most photogenic coffee shop in London. Taste matches the look.

items.name: Rosslyn Coffee
items.description: A serious coffee stop for City workers with precise espresso.
items.opinion: Serious coffee for serious people. Zero compromise on quality.

items.name: Attendant
items.description: A distinctive cafe in a converted Victorian public convenience — coffee and brunch done well.
items.opinion: Coffee served in a converted Victorian toilet. Only in London.

items.name: Prufrock Coffee
items.description: A respected speciality coffee bar for espresso and filter near Leather Lane.
items.opinion: The coffee nerd's coffee shop. World-class brewing in a relaxed space.

items.name: Ozone Coffee Roasters
items.description: Roastery-led coffee, excellent brunch, and a polished Shoreditch space.
items.mustTry: Smashed avo on sourdough and cold brew
items.opinion: Shoreditch brunch perfected. Great roastery, great food, great space.

items.name: Borough Market
items.description: The essential London food market for cheese, baked goods, oysters, and street food.
items.mustTry: Salt beef bagel from Monty's Deli
items.opinion: The greatest food market in the world. Full stop. Go hungry.

items.name: Maltby Street Market
items.description: Compact railway-arch market with creative street food and bakeries.
items.mustTry: Whatever the rotating special is that week
items.opinion: Borough Market's cooler, quieter little sibling. Locals only (until now).

items.name: Brick Lane Beigel Bake
items.description: A 24-hour East End institution for salt beef and smoked salmon bagels.
items.opinion: Open 24 hours. A £2.50 salt beef bagel at 3am is a London rite of passage.

items.name: Camden Market Food Stalls
items.description: Global street food with halal-friendly stalls. Ask individual vendors before ordering.
items.mustTry: Ethiopian injera from the world food section
items.opinion: More food choices than you can handle. Give yourself 2 hours minimum.

items.name: Gold Mine
items.description: A Bayswater favourite for roast duck, noodles, and Cantonese classics.
items.opinion: The best roast duck in London. No argument.

items.name: Mercato Metropolitano
items.description: Large indoor-outdoor food market with pizza, bao, desserts, and halal-friendly traders.
items.mustTry: Neapolitan pizza from the wood-fired oven
items.opinion: Huge, vibrant and full of options. One of London's best food halls.

items.name: Seven Dials Market
items.description: Central food hall for group dining, burgers, tacos, pasta, and pre-theatre bites.
items.opinion: Best central London food hall. 5 minutes from all the theatres.

items.name: Broadway Market
items.description: Neighbourhood Saturday market with pastries, street food, coffee, and London Fields nearby.
items.opinion: Peak London Saturday vibes. Beautiful people, great food, lovely park after.

items.name: Dishoom — 10% OFF
items.description: Show your TAP LONDON NFC souvenir for 10% off your total bill at any Dishoom branch in London.
items.opinion: Worth every penny even at full price.

items.name: Monmouth Coffee — Free Coffee
items.description: One free coffee with any food purchase at Monmouth Coffee Borough Market. Show your NFC souvenir.
items.opinion: London's best coffee — and now it's free.

items.name: Camden Market — 15% OFF
items.description: 15% discount at participating food stalls in Camden Market. Look for the TAP LONDON sticker.
items.opinion: Already cheap — now even cheaper.

items.name: Beigel Bake Brick Lane
items.description: London's most famous 24-hour bagel shop. Salt beef bagels are legendary — perfect after a night out. Cash preferred, always a queue but moves fast.

items.name: Yalla Yalla Soho
items.description: Lively Lebanese spot in the heart of Soho serving mezze and grills until late. Perfect for post-theatre or late night dinner.

items.name: BAO Borough
items.description: Cult Taiwanese bao restaurant. Small plates, incredible bao buns, open till late on weekends. Expect a wait but it's worth it.

items.name: Duck & Waffle
items.description: 40th floor restaurant open 24/7 with stunning London skyline views. Famous for its duck confit and waffle dish. Great for late night dining with a view.

items.name: Dirty Bones Shoreditch
items.description: Late night American comfort food with live DJ sets on weekends. Burgers, ribs and cocktails until 1am.

items.name: Franco Manca
items.description: Relaxed sourdough pizza chain loved by London families — casual, affordable, and always kid-friendly with high chairs and colouring available.

items.name: Giraffe
items.description: Bright, cheerful family restaurant chain with a varied menu for adults and kids, colouring sheets and high chairs at every branch.

items.name: Rainforest Cafe
items.description: Immersive jungle-themed restaurant with animatronic animals, thunderstorms and waterfalls — an unforgettable experience for kids.

items.name: Camille
items.description: Time Out's #1 restaurant in London for 2026. Chef Elliot Hashtroudi's French bistro fare has been called 'a triumph of imagination, talent and guts' — book well in advance.

items.name: St John
items.description: A London institution and pioneer of nose-to-tail British cooking. Ranked #3 in Time Out's 2026 list — its longevity and consistency remain unmatched.

items.name: Tiella
items.description: Southern Italian trattoria on Columbia Road that came second in Time Out's 2026 rankings — cooking that doesn't need to explain itself.

items.name: Quo Vadis
items.description: A Soho institution in a historic townhouse — refined modern British cooking in one of the neighbourhood's most storied dining rooms.

items.name: Osteria Vibrato
items.description: Lively Soho Italian featured in Time Out's 2026 top 50 — buzzy atmosphere and confident, seasonal cooking.

items.name: Govinda's
items.description: Beloved vegetarian institution in Soho, Time Out 2026-listed — simple, satisfying Indian vegetarian food at unbeatable prices.

items.name: Koya Ko
items.description: Hand-pulled udon specialist in Hackney, one of the borough's standout spots in Time Out's 2026 rankings.

items.name: Café Cecilia
items.description: Canalside neighbourhood restaurant in London Fields blending British and French influences — a Hackney favourite in Time Out's 2026 list.

items.name: Akub
items.description: Modern Palestinian cooking in Notting Hill, one of West London's standout entries in Time Out's 2026 top 50.

items.name: Normah's
items.description: Beloved homespun Malaysian spot inside Queensway market — ranked 5th in Time Out's 2026 list despite the market's closure being threatened.

items.name: Levan
items.description: One of South London's brightest culinary stars — confident, seasonal modern European cooking in Peckham, Time Out 2026-listed.

items.name: Kokum
items.description: Coastal Indian cooking in Dulwich, one of South London's Time Out 2026-listed standouts.

items.name: Rasa
items.description: Long-running South Indian vegetarian favourite in Stoke Newington — a Time Out 2026-listed neighbourhood treasure.

items.name: Chuku's
items.description: The UK's first Nigerian tapas restaurant, in Tottenham — bold, inventive small plates that earned a spot in Time Out's 2026 top 50.

items.name: Catalyst
items.description: Named one of the UK's best coffee shops for 2026 — Scandi-style space with in-house roasting, pop-up events and Friday cocktails.

items.name: Prufrock Coffee
items.description: One of the UK's best coffee shops for 2026, run by industry veterans with its own barista training centre — serious coffee, no pretension.

items.name: Carbon Kopi
items.description: New Zealand-founded roastery that relocated to Hammersmith — named among the UK's best coffee shops for 2026.

items.name: Specialty Cafetiere
items.description: Hackney coffee shop with a special water filtration system for the best possible brew — named one of the UK's top coffee shops for 2026.

items.name: Curators
items.description: Run by Send Coffee, a social enterprise providing barista training to people with disabilities — named among the UK's best coffee shops for 2026, great coffee with real purpose.

items.name: Caravan King's Cross
items.description: Half café, half restaurant with house-roasted beans and a global flavour menu — huge, lively, great for groups and first-time visitors.

items.name: Grind Soho
items.description: One of London's most recognisable modern café brands — stylish interiors, neon lights and precisely made coffee.

items.name: Esters
items.description: A quiet North London favourite with an inventive seasonal menu — roasted squash with labneh, rhubarb compote with house granola. Ideal for slow mornings.

items.name: Host Café
items.description: A converted church transformed into a coffee sanctuary — vaulted Gothic ceilings and stained glass make this one of London's most atmospheric cafés.

items.name: Friends of Ours at the Serpentine
items.description: One of the most enviable café settings in London — right on the edge of the Serpentine lake in Hyde Park, surrounded by parkland.

items.name: The Riding House Café
items.description: The definition of London brunch culture — leather banquettes, artisan cocktails and hearty plates like chorizo hash. Perfect for long, chatty brunches.

items.name: Tofu Vegan
items.description: Plant-based Chinese food that satisfies vegans and meat-eaters alike — Sichuan-style tofu, plump dumplings and crispy soy-protein 'wings'. Dishes from £8.

items.name: Club Mexicana
items.description: Bold plant-based Mexican street food since 2014 — Buffalo Mushroom Tacos and BBQ Short 'Rib' Tacos with a loud, sociable atmosphere built for groups.

items.name: Facing Heaven
items.description: Inventive plant-based regional Chinese cuisine named after a Sichuanese chili — natural wines, craft beers and baijiu cocktails alongside the food.

items.name: Jam Delish
items.description: Started on market stalls before securing a permanent home in Angel — classic Caribbean dishes made entirely plant-based, jerk 'chicken' and curry 'goat'.

items.name: Temple of Seitan
items.description: A well-known plant-based fried 'chicken' shop — burgers, wings and chicken pieces made from seitan, casual eat-with-your-hands vegan food.

items.name: The Spread Eagle
items.description: London's first fully vegan pub — a sustainable, plant-based take on classic British pub fare with global influences on traditional dishes.

items.name: Gauthier Soho
items.description: One of London's strongest options for a vegan date night — intimate setting, polished French service, and expert handling of dietary needs.

items.name: The Harwood Arms
items.description: London's only Michelin-starred pub, widely considered the city's finest Sunday roast — goose fat potatoes are the highlight. Book weeks ahead.
items.mustTry: Sunday roast with goose fat potatoes

items.name: The Bull & Last
items.description: A North London staple that treats Sunday roast with real seriousness — perfectly pink beef, fluffy Yorkshire puddings and seasonal sides.

items.name: Blacklock Soho
items.description: Famous for its unlimited 'all in' Sunday roast around £25 — exceptional value carved-at-the-table option in the heart of Soho.

items.name: Quality Chop House
items.description: A literally-named institution serving excellent quality meat — Mangalitza shoulder croquettes to start, sharing Suffolk lamb shoulder for Sunday lunch.

items.name: The Guinea Grill
items.description: A Mayfair institution — Yorkshire puddings 'the size of hubcaps', perfectly pink beef and gravy locals rave about, a weekly ritual for many.
items.mustTry: Roast beef with giant Yorkshire pudding

items.name: The Holly Bush
items.description: A cosy, atmospheric Hampstead pub known for crisp roast potatoes and a genuine old-London fireside feel — perfect winter Sunday lunch.

items.name: Elliot's
items.description: Borough Market darling applying its signature wood-fired philosophy to Sunday roasts — corn-fed chicken with porcini sauce, sirloin with bone marrow.

items.name: The Selkirk
items.description: A great-value neighbourhood pub famous for its golden, crunchy roast potatoes — budget-friendly Sunday roast from around £14-18.

items.name: Mangal II
items.description: Time Out 2026-listed Turkish institution — ultra-casual kebabs and hangover-friendly hummus that have wooed East Londoners for decades, reborn with sleek new energy since 2021.

items.name: Barrafina
items.area: Multiple Locations (Soho, Covent Garden, King's Cross)
items.description: Time Out's best tapas pick for tortilla — counter-only seating and expertly executed classic Spanish small plates across several London locations.

items.name: José
items.description: Time Out's pick for 'best holiday vibes' — a tiny standing-room tapas bar from acclaimed chef José Pizarro that transports you straight to Spain.

items.name: El Pirata of Mayfair
items.description: A longstanding Mayfair favourite for authentic Spanish tapas — regulars return every time they're in London, a genuine local institution.

items.name: Lokal
items.description: A cosy Turkish kitchen just moments from Oxford Circus — rooted in the idea of 'local by name, deeper by nature', great for a quick quality lunch.

items.name: Brother Marcus
items.description: Well-loved Mediterranean-Turkish spot in Spitalfields known for great breakfasts, friendly staff and consistently good food.

items.name: The Grain Store
items.description: A buzzy Chinese canteen in the old-school bit of King's Cross — Time Out 2026-listed for consistently good, unfussy cooking.

items.name: Lobos Meat & Tapas
items.description: High-quality, flavoursome Spanish tapas in the heart of Soho — ibérico pork, octopus and padrón peppers with menus that evolve seasonally.

items.name: Jacqueline at The Chancery Rosewood
items.description: Winner of La Liste's 2026 World's Best Afternoon Tea award — a dedicated tea sommelier guides you through infusions in this five-star Mayfair setting. From £105pp.

items.name: The Ritz London Afternoon Tea
items.description: The world's most famous tea service — tuxedo-clad servers in the iconic Palm Court, with the UK's only certified in-house Tea Master guiding 20+ loose-leaf blends. Dress code applies.
items.mustTry: Classic afternoon tea with Tea Master pairing

items.name: The Savoy Afternoon Tea
items.description: Served in the Gallery under a stained glass dome — including a Twilight Tea (6-9:30pm) with cocktail pairing for those who want tea a little later in the day.

items.name: Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon, Fortnum & Mason
items.description: A calm fourth-floor retreat above the famous food hall — quintessentially British afternoon tea from London's most iconic department store.

items.name: The Wolseley Afternoon Tea
items.description: Time Out's pick for best-value afternoon tea — grand European café-restaurant grandeur without the eye-watering five-star hotel prices.

items.name: The Goring Afternoon Tea
items.description: An intimate, classic tea experience with perfectly baked scones and endless top-ups of pastries — polished without ever feeling stuffy.

items.name: The Dilly London-Themed Tea
items.description: Best-value five-star hotel tea — a fun, London-landmark-themed afternoon tea served on a double-decker bus display. From £49pp.

items.name: Arôme
items.description: Good Food Guide 50 Best Bakeries 2026 winner — East Asian flavours meet French pastry, from hotdog croissants to miso bacon escargots and honey butter shokupan toast.

items.name: August Bakery
items.description: Named in British Baker's Baker's Dozen 2026 — a husband-and-wife bakery focused on substance over style, famous for miso sesame sourdough and kouign amann.

items.name: Chatsworth Bakehouse
items.description: A Crystal Palace cult favourite named in British Baker's Baker's Dozen 2026 — one of only two London bakeries recognised in the national ranking.

items.name: Little Bread Pedlar
items.description: Started delivering bread by cargo bike to devoted regulars, now with two permanent venues — French-imported butter and imaginative Danish pastries with rotating toppings.

items.name: Maltby Street Market
items.description: A small, vibrant street food market with quality stalls and producers — genuinely local, far less crowded than Borough Market a few streets away.

items.name: Arcade Food Hall
items.description: A buzzing indoor food hall — home to Gracey's pizza, Supa Ya ramen and excellent Thai restaurant Plaza Khao Gaeng, great when weather isn't cooperating.

items.name: MA/NA
items.description: London's most anticipated Japanese opening of 2026 — from the team behind Endo at the Rotunda. M5 Wagyu seared on Himalayan salt stone and an outstanding sushi programme.
items.mustTry: M5 Wagyu on Himalayan salt stone

items.name: Sollip
items.description: One of London's few Korean fine dining spots — a husband-and-wife team combining traditional Korean flame-and-smoke techniques with European training.

items.name: Miga
items.description: One of the highest-rated Korean restaurants in London — genuinely excellent modern Korean cooking in a relaxed Hackney setting.

items.name: Arang
items.description: Serving Korean BBQ since 2006 — seasoned spare ribs, kimchi pancakes and spicy squid, all washed down with plenty of soju.

items.name: New Malden Korean Town
items.description: Home to London's largest Korean community and the best-value authentic Korean food in the city — a direct train from Waterloo, well worth the journey.

items.name: Dopi
items.description: A casual Korean spot where soju, friends and good food come together — relaxed atmosphere perfect for groups.

items.name: AngloThai
items.description: A Michelin-starred Marylebone favourite blending British and Thai influences across tasting menus. Brixham crab with Exmoor caviar sits alongside coconut ash cream in a genuinely original take on both cuisines.
items.opinion: One of the more inventive fusion menus in London right now — book ahead.

items.name: KOL
items.description: A Michelin-starred Mexican restaurant using British-grown ingredients cooked with Mexican technique — a genuinely distinctive approach among London's fine dining scene.
items.opinion: Not a typical Mexican restaurant — expect a tasting-menu-style approach with British produce.

items.name: Kudu
items.description: A lively South African-inspired restaurant known for open-fire cooking and generous small plates. One of Peckham's most consistently booked-out spots.
items.opinion: Loud, fun, and the fire-cooked dishes are worth the wait for a table.

items.name: Trishna
items.description: A Michelin-starred coastal Indian restaurant known for precise, refined seafood dishes rooted in South Indian cooking traditions. Understated room, exceptional food.
items.opinion: Deceptively casual-looking from outside, but the cooking here is genuinely top-tier.

items.name: Fischer's
items.description: A grand Viennese-style café-restaurant serving schnitzels, strudel and central European classics in an elegant, old-world dining room right on Marylebone High Street.
items.opinion: Great for a leisurely lunch — the room itself is half the reason to go.

items.name: Bouchon Racine
items.description: A daily-changing French bistro menu inspired by Lyon, from chef Henry Harris. Honest, classic French cooking without pretension in a warm, unfussy dining room.
items.mustTry: Whatever's on the daily specials board
items.opinion: The kind of menu that changes daily and is always worth trusting — go with an open mind.

items.name: Maset
items.description: From the team behind Donostia and Lurra, Maset turns to southern coastal French cooking — pâtes au pistou, excellent steaks and a well-chosen cocktail list.
items.opinion: A calmer, less showy alternative to some of Marylebone's flashier openings.
